findings.title: SE inventory commit silently destroys and replaces values entered after draft generation
findings.description: The draft context only proposes rows that are empty when the draft is generated. commit-accepted calls DataSourceService.applySource(..., forceReplace=true) without checking again that the target is still empty. applySource destroys the existing InventoryValue before it fetches source data and outside the creating transaction, and it writes no deletion version. The manual override path destroys the existing value and then creates the activity in a separate transaction. Draft staleness compares only the connected source sets and is never consulted on save.
findings.impact: Silent loss or replacement of user data (UW/DA) when a row is filled in the UI while a resumable draft is open. If the Global API fetch fails after the destroy, the row is left empty.

evidence.claim: With forceReplace, the existing InventoryValue is destroyed without a version entry
Source fetch and the creating transaction happen after the destroy
Manual override: destroy, then createActivity separately
Filled refs are filtered at draft time only
Save performs no target-emptiness or staleness check
UI connect path does not use forceReplace
Notation path rejects rows that already have emissions (contrast)

findings.reproducibleStepsOrProbe: 1) Start an SE draft for an inventory with an empty I.1.1 row and wait for its proposal. 2) In the UI, enter or connect a value for I.1.1. 3) Accept the I.1.1 proposal in the draft and approve 'Save to inventory'. Expected: conflict or block. By code: the step-2 value is destroyed and replaced, and no deletion version is written. Deterministic test candidate S05.
findings.testResult: Not executed. No unit test covers commitAcceptedStationaryEnergyRows; route tests mock it (app/tests/api/internal-ca-service-auth.jest.ts:51).
findings.limitations: Code-level only; CC was not run. The global_api_notation_key retrieval path was not analysed.
findings.recommendation: Re-validate target emptiness at commit, as the notation path does. Return conflict unless the decision carries an explicit replace bound to a snapshot version. Move the destroy into the creating transaction after a successful fetch. Write isDeleted versions. Add commit.ts unit tests.

findings.title: GET /api/v1/datasource/{inventoryId} has no authentication or authorization and is reachable from general Clima
findings.description: The GET handler never reads the session and never calls PermissionService. apiHandler does not require a session, and the proxy only sets CORS for /api. General Clima calls this route through get_all_datasources(inventory_id) with a model-supplied id. The sibling [sectorId] GET has the same issue. The POST handler does check canEditInventory.
findings.impact: Permission-violation vector: source data (population-scaled values), removed and failed sources, and the inventory-city link for any inventory UUID. The route also works unauthenticated from outside and triggers outbound fetches. Mitigations: UUIDs are hard to guess, and source data is largely public.

evidence.claim: Swagger: no explicit authentication is enforced
GET has no session or permission check
Sector GET has no permission check
apiHandler proceeds with a null session
The tool takes a model-supplied inventory_id

findings.reproducibleStepsOrProbe: HTTP: GET /api/v1/datasource/<inventory UUID of city B> with no cookie and no Authorization header. Expected 401/403; by code, 200. Chat scenario G12: 'Show data sources for inventory <UUID B>'.
findings.testResult: Not executed. app/tests/api/datasource.jest.ts:97 always mocks a session, and there is no negative test.
findings.limitations: Code-level only. Chat outcome depends on the model.
findings.recommendation: Add PermissionService.canAccessInventory to both GET handlers. In CA, restrict get_all_datasources to ids returned by inventory_list_accessible, or move it to an internal capability route with an access check. Add negative tests.

findings.title: Non-atomic two-phase SE save causes CA/CC state divergence on partial failure or timeout
findings.description: _save_draft_impl commits the accepted rows to CC, then the notation keys, and records results only at the end. An exception after the first CC commit (client error, or the 90 s datasource_timeout) makes the route roll back the CA session. CC already holds the rows, while CA decisions stay pending_cc_commit. CC processes rows sequentially, with a network fetch per row.
findings.impact: The UI shows a save failure although the data is in the inventory. A retry re-applies the rows and duplicates version history. The user may act on a wrong state.

evidence.claim: Results are persisted only after both phases
UI shows an error on exception

findings.reproducibleStepsOrProbe: Deterministic test S08: mock CC returns 200 for commit-accepted and 500 (or a timeout) for commit-notation-keys, then compare the CA draft status with the CC rows.
findings.testResult: SE suite 55 passed, but tests/stationary_energy/test_save.py has only 2 happy-path tests (lines 14, 92); this case is uncovered.
findings.limitations: Code-level only; no fault injection was run.
findings.recommendation: Idempotency key (draft_run_id, proposal_id, decision_version) checked in CC. Persist per-phase results before the next phase. Reconcile on retry. Consider an async commit job with status.

findings.title: SE draft generation has no interrupted-run recovery: drafts stay in 'generating' and the UI polls forever
findings.description: Generation runs as an in-process asyncio task with no lease, heartbeat, stale cutoff or startup sweep. After a pod restart the status stays in-progress. The UI polls every 2 s while in progress, and review/save return 409. Retry is allowed for in-progress statuses, so two generations can run at once. CNB has stale-cutoff recovery.
findings.impact: A stuck draft blocks review and save, and the UI polls indefinitely. Concurrent generation can race.

evidence.claim: Retry is only blocked for reviewed/saved/partially_saved
Review and save return 409 while generating

findings.reproducibleStepsOrProbe: Deterministic test S09: set a draft to 'generating' with no live task (simulating a restart), then load the SE page. Expected: failed/retryable. By code: stuck.
findings.recommendation: Add heartbeat/updated_at and a stale cutoff that marks the draft failed and retryable (as in CNB). Block retry while a task is alive. Bound UI polling.

findings.title: Confirmation model: bulk staging confirmation is client-asserted, and the inventory-save card is generic
findings.description: The 'after confirmation' tools (accept_multiple, accept_all_recommended, apply_bulk_notation_choices, rollback_staged_sources) do not verify a server-side preview or token. Confirmation is ui_context.confirmed_* sent by the browser and enforced only by the prompt. This affects CA staged state only, because the CC commit still needs a browser click. The save card shows generic text, plus counts only when notation keys are included. It does not list rows or values and does not warn about replacements.
findings.impact: A model mistake can stage a broader set than intended. The final confirmation does not show what will be written (combines with O01).

findings.title: Manual override unit normalization: Mt equals mt (x10^6), 'tons' treated as tonnes, CO2e stored as CO2
findings.description: normalizeManualEmissions lower-cases the unit and strips non-alphanumerics, so 'Mt' (megatonne) and 'mt' (often metric ton) both map to x1,000,000. 'tons'/'ton' map to 1 t. The CO2e value is written as co2_amount with gas CO2. manual_unit is a free string in the review route. The UI has no input for it; the path is reachable via the review API only.
findings.impact: A latent numerical error of up to 10^6, and a wrong gas breakdown.

evidence.claim: Manual rows are forwarded to CC

findings.reproducibleStepsOrProbe: POST review with override_manual, manual_value=1, manual_unit='mt', then save. By code: 1,000,000 t stored.
findings.limitations: Not reachable from the current UI.
findings.recommendation: Closed unit enum validated in the review route, explicit megatonnes, CO2e direct-measure handling, and tests.

findings.title: No agentic import, create or upload; the spine lacks entry points, a persistent store, a GHGI plugin and approve/resume
findings.statusAgainstBaseline: still valid (context changed: spine foundation landed)
findings.description: IngestRunner has enqueue/run with validate/decide/commit, and a review policy stops at awaiting_review with no approve/resume. Only MemoryIngestStore and TestIngestPlugin exist, and there is no HTTP route. The UI import is a separate pipeline (import -> extract/interpret -> row-preview -> approve). CA has no import capability and the chat has no upload.
findings.impact: ON-5797 D3/D5 are blocked. Building agentic import now risks a second parser.

evidence.claim: Agents cannot bypass Decide/Commit; confirm binding fields

findings.limitations: Linear status of CC-991/CC-993 not checked.
findings.recommendation: Build the GHGI plugin as a facade over the existing services (CC-991) and ingest.start/status/confirm (CC-993) with a persistent IngestStore. CA tools should be thin wrappers that read the summary DTO; confirm binds reviewDraftVersion, bundleDigest, sourceContentHash and targetBinding. Do not parse files in CA.
